The components of ui-components also come for React and Svelte, built on the same scripts and style sheets as the Wicket ones, so a fix reaches all three. Below, the same form rendered by React and by Svelte: drop-downs, an autocomplete of colleagues and a list of all users that loads more of them as it scrolls. The framework renders the elements it owns, the shared scripts draw the components next to them, and the framework's state follows each choice.

Both load their data from resources this Wicket application mounts: the countries, named in the language of the session, and the users, the same as those of the JSON table. They take the colors of the theme chosen above.
